recipe: Sri Lankan coconut dhal (parippu) with turmeric-crisped tofu
servesNote: 2 portions — 904 kcal / 51 g protein each, VEGAN, and the cheapest dinner in the set at £1.43/portion. ⭐ Not another generic dahl: parippu is built on coconut and a hot-oil tempering poured over at the end.
adaptations: ⛔ THIS NEEDS A SHOP BEFORE IT CAN BE COOKED. Three things it treats as HELD are not in the house as of the 7 Sep stock check and were not on Tuesday's list: RED LENTILS (finished 26 Aug), CREAMED COCONUT, and CORNFLOUR. There is no working substitute for the lentils, and the tofu is not on the list either.
⭐ IF A TIN OF COCONUT MILK IS WHAT YOU HAVE: 150 ml replaces the creamed coconut sachet — half early at step 8, half off the heat at step 9. Skip the mug-and-boiling-water step entirely.

⚠️ WITHOUT CORNFLOUR THE TOFU WILL NOT CRISP, it will brown. The starch is what forms the crust. Plain flour is a poor stand-in here and rice flour is not in the house. If you are cooking this without it, accept browned tofu and do not extend the frying time trying to force a crust that cannot form.

⛔ THE HELD VEGETABLE STOCK STAYS OUT OF THIS ON PURPOSE, and not because it is missing — the lentils are cooked in plain water deliberately. Stock overpowers the lentil. Do not 'improve' it with the chicken stock cubes.

prep: Split the onion and the garlic before you start — half the onion diced and 2 cloves sliced for the dhal, half the onion sliced thinly and 2 cloves for the tempering. They go in at opposite ends of the cook and it is easy to use it all up front.
⛔ RINSE THE LENTILS, rubbing them between your fingers, until the water runs clear — about three changes. Unrinsed red lentils throw starchy scum and cook to a gluey rather than a creamy texture.

steps.text: Lentils into a pan with 500 ml COLD water, the diced half onion, 2 sliced garlic cloves, ¾ tsp turmeric, the cinnamon, black pepper and a good teaspoon of salt. Boil, skim the foam, then a gentle simmer with the lid ajar.

Cook, stirring now and then and scraping the base, until the lentils have completely lost their shape and a spoon dragged through the middle leaves a channel that fills back slowly. Top up with hot water if it tightens before the lentils have gone. ⚠️ Undercooked lentils keep a raw chalky bite — this is the one unanimous rule in the sources.
Tofu while they cook. Drain, pat both blocks thoroughly dry, cut into 2 cm cubes.

Toss the cubes with the cornflour, ¼ tsp turmeric and a good pinch of salt until each face is dusted and dry-looking. The starch is what forms the crust — without it you get browned tofu, not crisp tofu.
7 ml oil, medium-high, until it shimmers and flows easily. Tofu in a single layer with gaps — two batches if the pan is small.

⛔ Do not touch them. The tofu sticks at first and then releases itself once a crust has formed. Only turn each cube once it lifts cleanly and shows a deep golden face (2–3 min a side); do all the main faces. Onto a plate or rack, spread out — never a bowl or a heap, where it steams itself soft within a minute.

Coconut milk. Chop or crumble the creamed coconut into a mug, pour over 120 ml just-boiled water, stir until it has completely melted with no waxy specks left. ⛔ Creamed coconut set into a solid block will not dissolve in a simmering pan — it goes grainy.
HALF the coconut milk into the lentils, stirred through, bubbled very gently a minute or two to thicken.

⛔ Now take the pan OFF the heat and stir in the rest. From this point do not let it boil. Coconut milk added at the end and then boiled separates into oil and grain — the single failure mode Sri Lankan cooks warn about most.
Mash lightly — three or four presses with the back of a spoon, no more. Creamy with some texture remaining, not homogenised. Season; it will need more than you think.

⭐ THE TEMPERING (thel dala) — the step that makes it Sri Lankan, and it is done LAST. 8 ml oil in a small pan, medium. Sliced onion and the 2 remaining garlic cloves, until the onion is limp and its edges have gone properly brown and frizzled.

Cumin seeds and chilli powder, swirled about 20 seconds — ONLY until the seeds start to pop and smell toasty — then straight off the heat. ⚠️ Whole seeds and chilli go from fragrant to bitter in seconds; residual pan heat finishes them.

⭐ Pour the whole sizzling contents over the surface of the dhal, put a lid on the saucepan immediately, and leave it two minutes. Covering traps the aromatic steam and drives it down into the dhal instead of letting it escape into the kitchen. Then stir through, leaving a little on top.
Juice of half the lemon, off the heat. Taste again for salt and acid — dhal that tastes flat is nearly always short of salt first and acid second.
Rice: 90 g dry, 180 ml water, lidded, lowest heat until the water is gone and the surface is pitted with small holes, then 5 minutes off the heat still covered.

⭐ Serve the dhal over the rice with the crisp tofu scattered on top AT THE VERY LAST MOMENT, not stirred in. Stir it in early and it softens within a couple of minutes. Lemon wedges alongside. Maria's next-day lunch: reheat gently with a splash of water, stirring, and do not let it boil — the coconut can still split on the reheat. Keep the tofu in a separate container.
